newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: U.N. relief convoy brings food, medicine to Kabul.
newsitem.headline: U.N. relief convoy brings food, medicine to Kabul.

text.p: A U.N. convoy rolled into Kabul on Wednesday bringing food, medicine, fuel and shelter materials to the most needy residents of the Afghan capital captured last week by the Taleban Islamic militia.

Ismail Omar of the U.N. World Food Programme told Reuters 19 trucks from the Pakistani city of Peshawar brought 150 tonnes of wheat flour to feed the infirm, disabled and orphans among the Afghan capital's population of about one million.

"We are trying to deliver 3,000 to 3,500 tonnes of food a month to the Kabul area," Omar said. "Now we have sufficient stocks in Kabul and are building a buffer stock of 5,000 to 6,000 tonnes in case of emergency."

He said the WFP was delivering about one-fifth of the city's daily consumption, feeding about 180,000 people, but the United Nations expected to be feeding up to 240,000 needy residents during the coming winter.
Food and other supplies were also reaching Kabul every day by commercial trucks, he said, as the Taleban's capture of Kabul on Friday had reopened main roads into the city.
Fighting in the weeks before the takeover of Kabul had closed the main Peshawar-Kabul highway since September 11, when Taleban captured the eastern city of Jalalabad.
But some supplies had been coming in from the southern city of Kandahar and northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif right up until the night of the takeover.
The Taleban now control about three-quarters of Afghanistan. "The food supply situation has improved a lot and prices have come down," Ismail Omar said.
